database_summary: Mixed dataset containing (a) an aliens/persons domain with master, location and detail tables (aliens, alien_data, aliens_location, aliens_details), (b) city/country reference dimensions (cities, cities_countries, cities_currencies, cities_languages), (c) legislative/personnel tables (legislators, legislators_terms, legislation_date_dim), and (d) job-postings facts with job/skill dimensions & bridge (job_postings_fact, job_company, skills_dim, skills_job_dim). Data includes both descriptive attributes and measurable facts (e.g. salaries, populations). Several tables are likely at a one-row-per-entity grain; skills_job_dim is a many-to-many bridge linking jobs to skills and can multiply rows in joins. Foreign-key relationships are implied by matching id columns (e.g. job_postings_fact.company_id -> job_company.company_id, skills_job_dim.skill_id -> skills_dim.skill_id, skills_job_dim.job_id -> job_postings_fact.job_id).

accepted.name: job_postings_with_company
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  j.job_title_short,
  j.job_title,
  j.job_location,
  j.job_via,
  j.job_schedule_type,
  j.job_work_from_home,
  j.search_location,
  j.job_posted_date,
  j.job_no_degree_mention,
  j.job_health_insurance,
  j.job_country,
  j.salary_rate,
  j.salary_year_avg,
  j.salary_hour_avg,
  c.name AS name,
  c.link AS link,
  c.link_google AS link_google,
  c.thumbnail AS thumbnail
FROM job_postings_fact AS j
LEFT JOIN job_company AS c
  ON j.company_id = c.company_id
accepted.description: Denormalized job postings enriched with company metadata. Use when answering questions that need job attributes together with company name/link/thumbnail (e.g., salary by company, counts by company, location distributions). | Use for: Top companies by number of job postings; Average salary by company or company name; Job distribution by company and location; Identify companies offering remote work or health insurance

accepted.name: job_skills_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  j.job_title_short,
  j.job_title,
  j.job_location,
  j.job_posted_date,
  s.skill_id,
  d.skills AS skills,
  d.type AS type
FROM job_postings_fact AS j
JOIN skills_job_dim AS s
  ON j.job_id = s.job_id
LEFT JOIN skills_dim AS d
  ON s.skill_id = d.skill_id
accepted.description: Jobs joined to skill labels via the bridge table to expose skill text for each job. Use for skill-based aggregations, searching jobs requiring certain skills, or counting jobs per skill. | Use for: Count jobs requiring a given skill; Top skills by job count; Average salary for jobs requiring a particular skill

accepted.name: cities_with_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id,
  c.city_name,
  c.latitude,
  c.longitude,
  c.country_code_2,
  c.capital,
  c.population,
  c.insert_date,
  ct.country_id AS country_id,
  ct.country_name AS country_name,
  ct.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  ct.region AS region,
  ct.sub_region AS sub_region,
  ct.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region
FROM cities AS c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS ct
  ON c.country_code_2 = ct.country_code_2
accepted.description: Cities enriched with their country-level attributes (name, region, codes). Use when mapping cities to country metadata for regional analysis or currency/language join keys. | Use for: Largest cities by population in a region; Mapping cities to region/sub_region; Filter capitals or cities inserted after a date

accepted.name: cities_population_by_country
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  COUNT(city_id) AS city_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(population,0.0)) AS total_population_from_cities,
  AVG(COALESCE(population,0.0)) AS avg_city_population,
  MAX(COALESCE(population,0.0)) AS max_city_population,
  MIN(COALESCE(population,0.0)) AS min_city_population
FROM cities
GROUP BY country_code_2
accepted.description: Aggregated population metrics per country_code_2 based on cities. Use for country-level population summaries, average city size, and ranking countries by summed city populations. | Use for: Total city population by country; Average and maximum city size per country; Countries with many recorded cities

accepted.name: legislator_latest_term
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_start DESC) AS term_rank
FROM legislators_terms AS lt
accepted.description: Latest term per legislator ordered by term_start. Exposes a term_rank so callers can filter rank = 1 for the most recent term. Useful for current office holder, current party, state, or district lookups. | Use for: Who is the current legislator for a given bioguide or state/district; Current party or office for each legislator; Filter to most recent term per legislator

accepted.name: legislators_profile
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.id_bioguide,
  l.full_name,
  l.first_name,
  l.last_name,
  l.middle_name,
  l.nickname,
  l.suffix,
  l.birthday,
  l.gender,
  l.id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata,
  l.id_opensecrets,
  lt.term_id AS term_id,
  lt.term_start AS term_start,
  lt.term_end AS term_end,
  lt.term_type AS term_type,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.party AS party
FROM legislators AS l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM legislators_terms
) AS lt
  ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
  AND lt.term_start = (
    SELECT MAX(term_start) FROM legislators_terms AS lt2 WHERE lt2.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
  )
accepted.description: Legislator master rows with their most-recent term attributes (party, state, district) by joining to the latest term. Use for person-level queries that need current office info alongside biographical identifiers. | Use for: List legislators with current state and party; Join legislator biographical info to current office attributes; Filter legislators by party or state

accepted.name: alien_profiles
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  a.email,
  a.gender,
  a.type,
  a.birth_year AS birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  al.current_location AS current_location,
  al.state AS state,
  al.country AS country,
  al.occupation AS occupation
FROM aliens AS a
LEFT JOIN alien_data AS ad
  ON a.id = ad.id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location AS al
  ON ad.current_location = al.current_location
accepted.description: Alien profile view combining base aliens table with denormalized demographic/location/details present in alien_data, aliens_location, and aliens_details when keys align. Useful for analyses that need full profile attributes for each alien. | Use for: Profiles of aliens including location and aggression flag; Count aliens by favorite_food or feeding_frequency; Filter aliens by region/country/state or occupation

accepted.name: aliens_favorites_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(favorite_food, '') AS favorite_food,
  COALESCE(feeding_frequency, '') AS feeding_frequency,
  COUNT(id) AS alien_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(aggressive,0)) AS aggressive_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(id) = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE SUM(COALESCE(aggressive,0)) * 1.0 / COUNT(id) END AS aggressive_rate
FROM alien_data
GROUP BY favorite_food, feeding_frequency
accepted.description: Counts and aggression rates grouped by favorite_food and feeding_frequency. Useful for summaries of preferences and behavior among alien cohorts. | Use for: Which foods are associated with higher aggression?; Counts of aliens by feeding frequency; Compare aggression rates between feeding_frequency cohorts

accepted.name: job_postings_salary_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_id,
  company_id,
  job_country,
  job_title_short,
  salary_year_avg,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY job_country ORDER BY salary_year_avg DESC) AS salary_rank
FROM job_postings_fact
accepted.description: Rank job postings within each country by salary_year_avg (descending). Exposes salary_rank to let downstream queries pick top-N jobs per country or filter by rank ranges. | Use for: Top paid jobs per country; Identify percentile or rank of a specific job's salary within its country

accepted.name: legislation_calendar
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  month_name,
  day_of_month
FROM legislation_date_dim
accepted.description: Normalized date dimension for legislation-related dates exposing date components. Use for joining and filtering by month/day when analyzing legislation timelines. | Use for: Aggregate events by month or day from legislation-related datasets; Filter records by month_name or day_of_month
